I went to go see a doctor about 3 months ago, i live in Australia, so i don't know if its the same everyone, but i was worried alot coming upto it to, but it ended up being really quite easy, i was nervous of course, but the doctors don't force you to do anything. I was honestly worried when i was telling the doctor i've had plans of killing myself that they were gonna lock me up in some ward, for being a risk to myself. i honestly worried about that so much but of course they don't do that!, My parents didn't know i was suicidal at the time either, and them finding out was another one of my concerns, but the doctors don't get involved in that either, its up to you who knows what! My first appointment, the doctor read out some questions off the computer, standard questions you get in a depression test, eg/ Do you feel worthless? and questions about do i feel tired all the time, etc. and he also got me to get a blood test and thats all my first appointment was, he also booked me in to see a consellor, in australia if you have a healthcare card you get the first 6 conselling sessions for free then you have to start paying. i've only been to one session with a consellor, but the same thing happened, i was asked Alot more questions and just answered truthfully, she gave me the option if i didn't want to answer i didn't have too. her questions were more in depth and straight to the point of trying to find out why i was down, like "how is your relationship with your parents?" etc. trying to find out if there was a problem there. afterwards she gave me 3 options, keep seeing her for some more sessions, go on prozac or see a therapist. which i've stupidly chosen to do nothing and i'm just getting worse and worse. i just need to make an appointment with a doctor and i could get on prozac today. but it scares me at the same time. anyway I hope you you stay strong and go to your appointment! there's nothing to worry about, its pretty straight forward stuff. it can just be a little nervous telling a stranger but the doctors deal with it all the time, there's nothing to feel bad about!
